method: MIXED SOURCES. S1 and S2 are open NEDC pages fetched with curl and every claim from them is verbatim-checked with scripts/verify.py. A1 is the AMH therapeutic topic and the fluoxetine and lisdexamfetamine monographs, read under subscription and PARAPHRASED, with no stored quote and verdict licensed_source_not_quoted; dose claims flagged dose:true. NEDC links to eight jurisdictional admission documents rather than stating criteria, and NONE was retrieved, so no weight, heart rate, electrolyte or ECG admission threshold appears in this guideline -- recorded as input_unavailable because that is the operational core of the topic.

claims.claim: Psychological therapies have the greatest impact on symptom reduction and are first-line
claims.source_text: Psychological therapies are shown to have the greatest impact on eating disorder symptom reduction and other outcomes. Several outpatient psychological therapies have been identified as effective first-line treatments for eating disorders

claims.claim: Psychological therapy sits within multidisciplinary care and involves family and supports
claims.source_text: Psychological therapy is provided as part of a multidisciplinary care approach in combination with medical and nutritional management and recovery-based supports, and as much as possible, involves the person's family, carers, and supports

claims.claim: Minimum treatment team composition
claims.source_text: The treatment team at a minimum would comprise a mental health professional and a medical practitioner, and dietitians, other health professionals, and recovery support professionals may also be involved

claims.claim: Treatment and setting are matched to disorder type, severity and readiness
claims.source_text: Treatment type and the setting in which the treatment is provided should be matched according to the type of eating disorder, the severity of the problem and the person's goals, values and readiness for change

claims.claim: CBT-E is transdiagnostic and manualised
claims.source_text: Enhanced Cognitive Behavioural Therapy - Enhanced (CBT-E) (1) is a manualised psychological treatment that is “transdiagnostic”. This means that it is designed to address the key features of anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa, binge eating disorders and other specified feeding and eating disorders

claims.claim: CBT-E targets eating habits and attitudes to shape and weight
claims.source_text: CBT-E focuses on addressing the characteristic disruptions in eating habits and attitudes to shape and weight that keep an eating disorder in place

claims.claim: CBT-E session counts differ by weight status
claims.source_text: With people who are not significantly underweight, CBT-E generally involves an initial assessment appointment followed by 20 50-minute treatment sessions over 20 weeks. With people who are underweight treatment needs to be longer, often involving about 40 sessions over 40 weeks

claims.claim: CBT-E is for adults 18 and over with moderate to severe disorders
claims.source_text: CBT-E is a leading evidence-based psychological treatment for adults (18+) with moderate to severe

claims.claim: Limited CBT-E evidence in young people
claims.source_text: While there have been limited studies on CBT-E efficacy in young people, there is some evidence for the efficacy of CBT-E with family support for older adolescents

claims.claim: FBT is the Maudsley Model and empowers parents
claims.source_text: Family Based Treatment (FBT) (7) for eating disorders is commonly known as The Maudsley Model and is used to treat adolescents with Anorexia … FBT is a manualised treatment that aims to empower the family, namely the parents, to bring about recovery in their child with an eating disorder within their home environment

claims.claim: FT-BN is first line for bulimia nervosa in children and young people
claims.source_text: Bulimia-nervosa-focused family therapy (FT-BN) is recommended as the first line treatment for bulimia nervosa in children and young people

claims.claim: FBT phase one is parent-led refeeding
claims.source_text: Phase one focuses on nutritional and weight restoration. Parents are charged with the responsibility of refeeding their child and containing eating disorder behaviours. The clinician coaches parents to manage problematic eating disorder behaviours and brainstorm barriers to refeeding

claims.claim: FBT phase two returns control of eating to the adolescent
claims.source_text: Phase two Focuses on returning control of eating to the adolescent. Parents gradually hand back control of eating to the young person whilst managing any lapses

claims.claim: FBT phase three addresses adolescent issues and completion
claims.source_text: Phase three addresses adolescent issues and treatment completion. The final stage assumes that the young person is weight restored and in control of their eating behaviours

claims.claim: FBT eligibility is under 19 with three years or less of illness
claims.source_text: FBT is suitable for young people under the age of 19 who have been experiencing an eating disorder for three years or less

claims.claim: FBT typically runs over 12 months
claims.source_text: FBT treatment typically occurs over a 12-month period, although treatment time varies

claims.claim: Therapies are most efficacious delivered by an eating disorders-informed clinician
claims.source_text: Evidence-based outpatient therapies delivered by an eating disorders-informed clinician are considered most efficacious

claims.claim: FBT requires approved training and ongoing supervision
claims.source_text: FBT should be delivered by a mental health clinician who has completed introductory eating disorders training and approved training in FBT with ongoing supervision in FBT

claims.claim: NEDC refers to the ANZAED standards
claims.source_text: the ANZAED eating disorder treatment principles and general clinical practice and training standards and the ANZAED practice and training standards for mental health professionals providing eating disorder treatment

claims.claim: Treatment occurs across outpatient, inpatient, residential and day programs
claims.source_text: Treatment for an eating disorder can take place within a variety of settings across outpatient, inpatient, residential or day programs, and involves a multidisciplinary team of providers

claims.claim: Treatment can usually be outpatient
claims.source_text: Eating disorder treatment can usually be provided on an outpatient basis. Outpatient treatment is treatment that takes place within a setting that does not involve an overnight stay

claims.claim: Australian options include private and public
claims.source_text: Treatment options for people experiencing an eating disorder within Australia include both private and public options

claims.claim: Clinicians should use state guidelines where they exist and local ones where they do not
claims.source_text: A number of jurisdictions have developed state/terr itory -wide hospital admission guidelines for eating disorders. Clinicians should refer to the relevant state/territory guidelines where these exist to determine if a patient meets the criteria for either a medical or psychiatric admission. In the absence of state/territory guidelines, clinicians should refer to local service-level guidelines

claims.claim: NT, SA, TAS and VIC have no statewide admission guidelines
claims.source_text: NT   No statewide admission guidelines … SA   No statewide admission guidelines … TAS   No statewide admission guidelines … VIC   No statewide admission guidelines

claims.claim: Named jurisdictional admission guidelines
claims.source_text: Canberra Health Services Guideline - Adults with Eating Disorders – Medical Management of Inpatients … Guidelines for the Admission of Children and Young People with an Eating Disorder (2025) … Queensland Health Guideline Eating Disorders: Inpatient care on adult wards (2026) … WA Eating Disorders Outreach & Consultation Service (WAEDOCS) Eating Disorders: the Management of Youth and Adults - a Quick Reference Guide (2019)

claims.claim: A multidisciplinary approach is important and psychological treatments including cognitive behaviour therapy, interpersonal psychotherapy and, in anorexia nervosa, family psychotherapy for children and adolescents are keys in management
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Eating disorders' (Psychotropic drugs > Antidepressants), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: SSRIs particularly fluoxetine have been used, with very little evidence for effectiveness in anorexia nervosa, good evidence of a small effect in bulimia nervosa, and some evidence in binge eating disorders
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Eating disorders' (Psychotropic drugs > Antidepressants), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: In bulimia nervosa the SSRI dose needed is often higher than for depression
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Eating disorders' (Psychotropic drugs > Antidepressants), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Lisdexamfetamine may be a second line option in binge eating disorder
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Eating disorders' (Psychotropic drugs > Antidepressants), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMH directs readers to the National Eating Disorders Collaboration for further information
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Eating disorders' (Psychotropic drugs > Antidepressants), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Fluoxetine for bulimia nervosa is oral 20 mg once daily increasing as indicated to 60 to 80 mg daily
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monographs fluoxetine and lisdexamfetamine, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Lisdexamfetamine for binge eating disorder in adults is oral 30 mg once each morning, increased by 20 mg at intervals of at least a week to a usual dose of 50 or 70 mg daily, maximum 70 mg daily, with an initial treatment period of 12 weeks
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monographs fluoxetine and lisdexamfetamine, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22
